notes: What it is (class default): a long-term, population-typical Ṁ for a typical star of its class and radius (no X-ray measurement of the star). Never the star's current wind; single-epoch catalog fluxes, with the cycle/flare spread inside the band.

The band is ≈ 68 %: on the 22 astrospheric detections' leave-one-out residuals the regime bands cover 15 — about 1 star in 3 falls outside, with residuals up to 1.5 dex from the line (≤ 0.3 dex beyond a band edge); the widths were set with those residuals in view (a calibration, not an independent test); the widened, class-default and non-detection bands are model constructions with no separate coverage test.

How much the X-ray tier knows: it beats a class default by ≈ 9 % in dex overall (leave-one-out rms 0.855 vs 0.944). By regime (line vs class default): log F_X < 4.7 — 0.20 vs 0.45 dex (n = 5); 4.7–6.0 — 0.88 vs 1.02 (n = 13); above 6.0 — 1.21 vs 1.12 (n = 4: no gain — there a single F_X carries no more information than "active star").

The quiet band is GK-calibrated: the six detections below log F_X 4.7 are G/K stars and the Sun; the 4.85 quiet edge takes in one M dwarf, GJ 173 (log F_X 4.81), which sits +0.50 above the line, outside +0.30.
K and M stars split in the mid regime: K dwarfs sit ≈ +0.8 dex above the line, M dwarfs ≈ 0 — equally consistent with one line (LRT p = 0.72), so one line is used.

The intercept is a method choice: using the upper limits (censoring) lowers it 0.18 dex vs a plain fit (×1.5 in Ṁ, ×1.23 in a wall); it is WB-derived (Wood publishes a slope only; Wood's 0.77 lies inside this fit's slope 68 % CI).

eRASS1 fluxes of soft, quiet stars may read low: a one-sided term ≲ 0.3 dex in F_X, so the point Ṁ may read up to 0.18 dex low (0.3 × the slope 0.592; the central wall up to ≈ 19 % low — the true wall up to ≈ 23 % larger) — inside the band's upper half in every regime; it is not added to the band (were it added in quadrature to the quiet band's +0.30, that wall edge would move ≈ 6 %); the conversion is untested below log F_X 5.5.
The typical point sits above the class's predicted-rate median by 0.08–0.27 dex.

Radius limits: M7–M9 have fewer than 3 catalog radii within 10 pc and take the M6 median (0.1275 R⊙), likely too large for M8–M9 (by roughly 10–25 % — an unpinned estimate) — ≲ 0.08 dex in an X-ray-tier Ṁ (the radius enters F_X too: Ṁ ∝ R^(2 × (1 − 0.592)) = R^0.82) but up to ≈ 0.19 dex in a class-default Ṁ (Ṁ ∝ R²); in a close pair a catalog cross-match can give a star its companion's radius, which the 0.3-dex check does not catch when the two are similar (α Cen B carries α Cen A's 1.225 R⊙ in the W4 pull; flagged radius_pair_ambiguous) — supply --radius-rsun where it matters.

notes: What it is (class default): a long-term, population-typical Ṁ for a typical star of its class and radius (no X-ray measurement of the star). Never the star's current wind; single-epoch catalog fluxes, with the cycle/flare spread inside the band.

The band is ≈ 68 %: on the 22 astrospheric detections' leave-one-out residuals the regime bands cover 15 — about 1 star in 3 falls outside, with residuals up to 1.5 dex from the line (≤ 0.3 dex beyond a band edge); the widths were set with those residuals in view (a calibration, not an independent test); the widened, class-default and non-detection bands are model constructions with no separate coverage test.

How much the X-ray tier knows: it beats a class default by ≈ 9 % in dex overall (leave-one-out rms 0.855 vs 0.944). By regime (line vs class default): log F_X < 4.7 — 0.20 vs 0.45 dex (n = 5); 4.7–6.0 — 0.88 vs 1.02 (n = 13); above 6.0 — 1.21 vs 1.12 (n = 4: no gain — there a single F_X carries no more information than "active star").

The quiet band is GK-calibrated: the six detections below log F_X 4.7 are G/K stars and the Sun; the 4.85 quiet edge takes in one M dwarf, GJ 173 (log F_X 4.81), which sits +0.50 above the line, outside +0.30.
K and M stars split in the mid regime: K dwarfs sit ≈ +0.8 dex above the line, M dwarfs ≈ 0 — equally consistent with one line (LRT p = 0.72), so one line is used.

The intercept is a method choice: using the upper limits (censoring) lowers it 0.18 dex vs a plain fit (×1.5 in Ṁ, ×1.23 in a wall); it is WB-derived (Wood publishes a slope only; Wood's 0.77 lies inside this fit's slope 68 % CI).

eRASS1 fluxes of soft, quiet stars may read low: a one-sided term ≲ 0.3 dex in F_X, so the point Ṁ may read up to 0.18 dex low (0.3 × the slope 0.592; the central wall up to ≈ 19 % low — the true wall up to ≈ 23 % larger) — inside the band's upper half in every regime; it is not added to the band (were it added in quadrature to the quiet band's +0.30, that wall edge would move ≈ 6 %); the conversion is untested below log F_X 5.5.
The typical point sits above the class's predicted-rate median by 0.08–0.27 dex.

Radius limits: M7–M9 have fewer than 3 catalog radii within 10 pc and take the M6 median (0.1275 R⊙), likely too large for M8–M9 (by roughly 10–25 % — an unpinned estimate) — ≲ 0.08 dex in an X-ray-tier Ṁ (the radius enters F_X too: Ṁ ∝ R^(2 × (1 − 0.592)) = R^0.82) but up to ≈ 0.19 dex in a class-default Ṁ (Ṁ ∝ R²); in a close pair a catalog cross-match can give a star its companion's radius, which the 0.3-dex check does not catch when the two are similar (α Cen B carries α Cen A's 1.225 R⊙ in the W4 pull; flagged radius_pair_ambiguous) — supply --radius-rsun where it matters.

notes: log F_X 6.040 is within 0.15 dex of the mid/active regime edge (log F_X 6); the neighbouring mid regime's band would be -0.887 / +1.227 dex
What it is (X-ray tier): a long-term, population-typical Ṁ for a star at that X-ray flux. Never the star's current wind; single-epoch catalog fluxes, with the cycle/flare spread inside the band.

The band is ≈ 68 %: on the 22 astrospheric detections' leave-one-out residuals the regime bands cover 15 — about 1 star in 3 falls outside, with residuals up to 1.5 dex from the line (≤ 0.3 dex beyond a band edge); the widths were set with those residuals in view (a calibration, not an independent test); the widened, class-default and non-detection bands are model constructions with no separate coverage test.

How much the X-ray tier knows: it beats a class default by ≈ 9 % in dex overall (leave-one-out rms 0.855 vs 0.944). By regime (line vs class default): log F_X < 4.7 — 0.20 vs 0.45 dex (n = 5); 4.7–6.0 — 0.88 vs 1.02 (n = 13); above 6.0 — 1.21 vs 1.12 (n = 4: no gain — there a single F_X carries no more information than "active star").

The quiet band is GK-calibrated: the six detections below log F_X 4.7 are G/K stars and the Sun; the 4.85 quiet edge takes in one M dwarf, GJ 173 (log F_X 4.81), which sits +0.50 above the line, outside +0.30.
K and M stars split in the mid regime: K dwarfs sit ≈ +0.8 dex above the line, M dwarfs ≈ 0 — equally consistent with one line (LRT p = 0.72), so one line is used.

The intercept is a method choice: using the upper limits (censoring) lowers it 0.18 dex vs a plain fit (×1.5 in Ṁ, ×1.23 in a wall); it is WB-derived (Wood publishes a slope only; Wood's 0.77 lies inside this fit's slope 68 % CI).

eRASS1 fluxes of soft, quiet stars may read low: a one-sided term ≲ 0.3 dex in F_X, so the point Ṁ may read up to 0.18 dex low (0.3 × the slope 0.592; the central wall up to ≈ 19 % low — the true wall up to ≈ 23 % larger) — inside the band's upper half in every regime; it is not added to the band (were it added in quadrature to the quiet band's +0.30, that wall edge would move ≈ 6 %); the conversion is untested below log F_X 5.5.
The typical point sits above the class's predicted-rate median by 0.08–0.27 dex.

Radius limits: M7–M9 have fewer than 3 catalog radii within 10 pc and take the M6 median (0.1275 R⊙), likely too large for M8–M9 (by roughly 10–25 % — an unpinned estimate) — ≲ 0.08 dex in an X-ray-tier Ṁ (the radius enters F_X too: Ṁ ∝ R^(2 × (1 − 0.592)) = R^0.82) but up to ≈ 0.19 dex in a class-default Ṁ (Ṁ ∝ R²); in a close pair a catalog cross-match can give a star its companion's radius, which the 0.3-dex check does not catch when the two are similar (α Cen B carries α Cen A's 1.225 R⊙ in the W4 pull; flagged radius_pair_ambiguous) — supply --radius-rsun where it matters.

flag active_bimodal: this star's F_X is in the active regime (≥ 6.0), where the four astrospheric detections split into a weak mode (3 of the 4) 0.7–1.4 dex below the line and a strong mode (1 of the 4) ≈ 1.4 dex above it — what Wood 2021 calls "a hint of possible bimodality". The point is the line, which neither mode sits on; the ±1.2-dex band spans both.

flag extrapolated: an M4.5 or later star lies outside the fit's calibration: 0.2 dex is added in quadrature to both band edges — a nominal term (no M4.5+ astrospheric detection exists, so the extrapolation is unsized).

notes: What it is (class default): a long-term, population-typical Ṁ for a typical star of its class and radius (no X-ray measurement of the star). Never the star's current wind; single-epoch catalog fluxes, with the cycle/flare spread inside the band.

The band is ≈ 68 %: on the 22 astrospheric detections' leave-one-out residuals the regime bands cover 15 — about 1 star in 3 falls outside, with residuals up to 1.5 dex from the line (≤ 0.3 dex beyond a band edge); the widths were set with those residuals in view (a calibration, not an independent test); the widened, class-default and non-detection bands are model constructions with no separate coverage test.

How much the X-ray tier knows: it beats a class default by ≈ 9 % in dex overall (leave-one-out rms 0.855 vs 0.944). By regime (line vs class default): log F_X < 4.7 — 0.20 vs 0.45 dex (n = 5); 4.7–6.0 — 0.88 vs 1.02 (n = 13); above 6.0 — 1.21 vs 1.12 (n = 4: no gain — there a single F_X carries no more information than "active star").

The quiet band is GK-calibrated: the six detections below log F_X 4.7 are G/K stars and the Sun; the 4.85 quiet edge takes in one M dwarf, GJ 173 (log F_X 4.81), which sits +0.50 above the line, outside +0.30.
K and M stars split in the mid regime: K dwarfs sit ≈ +0.8 dex above the line, M dwarfs ≈ 0 — equally consistent with one line (LRT p = 0.72), so one line is used.

The intercept is a method choice: using the upper limits (censoring) lowers it 0.18 dex vs a plain fit (×1.5 in Ṁ, ×1.23 in a wall); it is WB-derived (Wood publishes a slope only; Wood's 0.77 lies inside this fit's slope 68 % CI).

eRASS1 fluxes of soft, quiet stars may read low: a one-sided term ≲ 0.3 dex in F_X, so the point Ṁ may read up to 0.18 dex low (0.3 × the slope 0.592; the central wall up to ≈ 19 % low — the true wall up to ≈ 23 % larger) — inside the band's upper half in every regime; it is not added to the band (were it added in quadrature to the quiet band's +0.30, that wall edge would move ≈ 6 %); the conversion is untested below log F_X 5.5.
The typical point sits above the class's predicted-rate median by 0.08–0.27 dex.

Radius limits: M7–M9 have fewer than 3 catalog radii within 10 pc and take the M6 median (0.1275 R⊙), likely too large for M8–M9 (by roughly 10–25 % — an unpinned estimate) — ≲ 0.08 dex in an X-ray-tier Ṁ (the radius enters F_X too: Ṁ ∝ R^(2 × (1 − 0.592)) = R^0.82) but up to ≈ 0.19 dex in a class-default Ṁ (Ṁ ∝ R²); in a close pair a catalog cross-match can give a star its companion's radius, which the 0.3-dex check does not catch when the two are similar (α Cen B carries α Cen A's 1.225 R⊙ in the W4 pull; flagged radius_pair_ambiguous) — supply --radius-rsun where it matters.

A combined-wind band: the band sums the members' band-edge rates — the merged system's own band when they share one blended F_X; with separate F_X it assumes their residuals move together, and for independent residuals the pair's upper edge could lie up to ≈ ×1.3 further out in the wall (mid, active and class-default bands; in the quiet band the summed edge is conservative).
